title: Strings, Immutability & Encoding
description: Strings store sequence characters as immutable bytes/code points using UTF-8 / UTF-16 encodings.

codeExamples.python:
text = 'Hello World'
upper_text = text.upper()
split_words = text.split(' ')
joined_text = '-'.join(split_words)
print(f'Upper: {upper_text}, Words: {split_words}, Joined: {joined_text}')

quiz.question: What does String Immutability mean in Python and Java?
options: Once a string object is created in memory, its text content cannot be altered in-place. Modifying a string creates a brand new string object in Heap RAM.
Strings automatically delete themselves after 1 minute.
Strings cannot be passed into functions.
quiz.explanation: String immutability ensures security, hashability, and thread safety. Modifying a string generates a new memory object.

interviewQuestions.q: 01. Why are Strings Immutable in Python and Java?
interviewQuestions.a: Immutability provides thread safety, allows string interning (reusing identical string literals in memory), and ensures strings can safely be used as dictionary keys (hash value remains constant).

interviewQuestions.q: 02. What is String Interning and how does it save RAM memory?
interviewQuestions.a: String Interning reuses a single Heap object for identical string literals (e.g. `a = 'hello'`, `b = 'hello'`). `a is b` evaluates to True because both point to the same interned address.

interviewQuestions.q: 03. What is the performance pitfall of string concatenation inside a loop (`s += char`)?
interviewQuestions.a: Because strings are immutable, `s += char` inside an N-iteration loop creates N intermediate string objects, taking quadratic O(N²) time. Use `''.join(char_list)` or `StringBuilder` for linear O(N) performance.

interviewQuestions.q: 04. What is Unicode (ASCII, UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32) encoding?
interviewQuestions.a: ASCII uses 7 bits (128 characters). Unicode maps 1,114,112 code points. UTF-8 is a variable-width encoding (1 to 4 bytes per character) backward compatible with ASCII.

interviewQuestions.q: 05. What is the difference between `ord()` and `chr()` in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: `ord('A')` returns the integer Unicode code point (65). `chr(65)` converts the integer code point back into its character string representation ('A').

interviewQuestions.q: 06. How does Python 3.3+ (PEP 393) flexible string representation work internally?
interviewQuestions.a: Python dynamically picks 1-byte (Latin-1), 2-byte (UCS-2), or 4-byte (UCS-4) memory layouts per string depending on the highest code point inside, optimizing memory usage.

interviewQuestions.q: 07. What is string slicing complexity in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: In Python 3, string slicing `s[start:stop]` allocates and copies characters into a new string object in O(K) time, where K is slice length.

interviewQuestions.q: 08. What is the difference between `str` vs `bytes` in Python 3?
interviewQuestions.a: `str` stores human-readable Unicode text code points. `bytes` stores raw 8-bit binary data (`b'hello'`). Convert using `text.encode('utf-8')` and `raw_bytes.decode('utf-8')`.

interviewQuestions.q: 09. What is String Matching Algorithms (KMP, Rabin-Karp, Boyer-Moore)?
interviewQuestions.a: Naïve string pattern matching takes O(N*M) time. Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) preprocesses pattern prefix functions to achieve O(N) linear time search.

interviewQuestions.q: 10. What is Anagram Detection algorithm and what is its time complexity?
interviewQuestions.a: Two strings are anagrams if sorting both returns equal strings (O(N log N)) or if frequency hash maps of both character counts match (O(N) linear time).

interviewQuestions.q: 11. What is Palindrome Verification algorithm?
interviewQuestions.a: Check if a string reads the same forward and backward (`s == s[::-1]`) or use two pointers moving inward from index 0 and N-1 in O(N) time and O(1) space.

interviewQuestions.q: 12. What is Levenshtein Edit Distance algorithm?
interviewQuestions.a: A dynamic programming algorithm computing the minimum number of single-character edits (insertions, deletions, substitutions) required to transform one string into another.

interviewQuestions.q: 13. How does f-string (`f"{var}"`) formatting compare to `%` and `.format()` in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: f-strings (PEP 498) evaluate expressions at runtime in compiled bytecode, rendering faster and more readably than `.format()` or `%` formatting.

interviewQuestions.q: 14. How does `strip()`, `lstrip()`, and `rstrip()` work?
interviewQuestions.a: Removes leading and trailing whitespace characters (or specified character sets) from string ends.

interviewQuestions.q: 15. What is the difference between `find()` vs `index()` in Python strings?
interviewQuestions.a: `find('sub')` returns `-1` if substring is not found. `index('sub')` raises a `ValueError` exception if substring is missing.

interviewQuestions.q: 16. How does Regular Expression (`re` module) work on strings?
interviewQuestions.a: Regex compiles pattern strings into finite state automata (NFA/DFA) to match complex text patterns, sub-string extractions, and replacements.

interviewQuestions.q: 17. What is String Pool in Java JVM Heap?
interviewQuestions.a: A special storage area inside Java Heap RAM where string literals are cached to avoid creating duplicate string instances.

interviewQuestions.q: 18. What is Trie (Prefix Tree) data structure for autocomplete search?
interviewQuestions.a: A tree-based data structure storing string characters as node edges, providing fast O(L) prefix lookup for search autocompletion.

interviewQuestions.q: 19. What is String Reversal in-place in languages with mutable strings (C/C++)?
interviewQuestions.a: In C++, `std::swap(str[i], str[n-i-1])` reverses strings in-place without auxiliary memory.

interviewQuestions.q: 20. What are production best practices when working with Strings?
interviewQuestions.a: Use `''.join()` for aggregating multiple strings, explicitly specify encoding `encoding='utf-8'` when reading files, and sanitize string inputs against SQL/XSS injections.
